- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.
- In cases of sustained upward momentum (sentiment > 0.5 for 3+ days), model tends to overestimate — apply mean reversion bias toward prior 5-day average.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.4), model often misreads direction — adjust forecast by 3–5% downward in the next 3 periods.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if recent history shows volatility > 2% per day, reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply a 1–2 period lag correction to align with actual mean.
